main.description: An append-only lifecycle statement about a version or project. State changes are expressed by superseding records, never by editing or deleting prior ones; current state is the latest live same-DID status record for a subject, and absence means active. Yank means do-not-newly-adopt, never ceases-to-exist. The documented norm is yank, don't delete; retraction is the testimonied last resort for mistakes — a retracted status written in the same commit as its subject's deletion, so the removal itself stays in append-only history.

subject.description: The software.release.version or software.release.project this statement is about. Must be same-DID.

status.description: Lifecycle state. yanked: do not newly adopt (explicit-version access keeps working, channel resolution never answers with it, updaters fail static). active: supersedes a prior state (unyank). deprecated: still valid for resolution, always surfaced with a warning. archived: for project subjects. retracted: testimony that the subject was deliberately deleted by the key-holder — written in the same commit as the deletion, its subject intentionally dangling thereafter. Records with unrecognized values are ignored for state derivation.

kind.description: Optional machine-facing reason category. Open vocabulary.
